01

Welcome to live mode

A whole life. A playable character.

A familiar kind of chaos, built on the rules your table already knows.

You were watering a suspicious plant. Then the rocket exploded. Now there is a wizard asking about your floating diamond, and you have bills in two dimensions.

This handbook brings the everyday chaos of The Sims 4 into a fantasy campaign. Your Sim is a complete adventurer: useful in a fight, free to make choices, and occasionally very upset about the chairs.

Rules foundation5e · 2024 revision
Character chassisNormal D&D class
Everything Sims-specificHomebrew adaptation

Your first five minutes

  1. 01
    Choose one species package.

    Use the ordinary Sim below, one occult replacement, or an approved official species with Sim flavor. Pick one route.

  2. 02
    Build a normal adventurer.

    Choose a background and class. Take ability increases, feats, gear, saves, and proficiencies only from the rules that grant them.

  3. 03
    Give them a life outside initiative.

    Choose an aspiration, two personality traits, a home world, and one thing they miss. The microwave is a valid answer.

  4. 04
    Agree on the optional modules.

    Moods are descriptive by default. The needs checklist is optional. Magic items and monsters belong to the DM.

Homebrew ruleNew mechanics written for this handbook.Official reskinAn existing rule with a new name; its mechanics stay intact.FlavorStory and personality, without extra bonuses.

A campaign about building a life

The Sims premise works best when the party has something worth returning to: a rented house, a tavern room, a repaired workshop, or a little garden behind a guildhall. Adventures can provide the money, relationships, and discoveries that change that home. A dungeon is more interesting when the broken oven waiting afterward belongs to somebody you care about.

Use three scales of story. In a scene, the Sim wants something immediate: a quiet meal, a useful clue, a rescue. Across an adventure, they pursue a concrete milestone: repair a portal component or earn a community’s trust. Across the campaign, their aspiration changes what a satisfying life would mean. The Knowledge Sim may discover that returning home matters less than the people helping them do it.

The rhythm of a session

  1. Begin with an ordinary concern. A letter arrives, a neighbor needs help, or the house has become too quiet. Let one person describe a small detail of the household.
  2. Give that concern an adventurous consequence. The letter crossed a sealed portal; the neighbor’s missing pet is in a forbidden greenhouse; the quiet house is quiet because every chair has vanished.
  3. Play the actual adventure. Follow the campaign’s normal exploration, combat, resource, and advancement rules. Sims flavor explains the characters’ responses.
  4. Return with a change. A new friend, a damaged relationship, a repaired room, or an uncomfortable truth gives the next adventure somewhere to begin.
A small opening scene

The party’s landlord needs the cellar inspected before the building inspector arrives. Someone has been leaving tiny hats outside the boiler room. The Rogue recognizes a lock that has been opened from the inside; the Druid notices unusual roots; the Fighter hears deliberate scraping. The important discovery is available as soon as they investigate. Checks can determine how quickly and safely they understand it, rather than whether the session gets to happen.

For a serious campaign, let the humor come from specific people and mundane expectations meeting extraordinary circumstances. Your Sim can be frightened and brave at the same time. They can miss their favorite mug without treating the death of a companion as a sitcom beat.

02

Create a Sim

Start with a person. Add a plumbob.

One species package, one background, one class. Plenty of room for bad decisions.

Homebrew species

The ordinary Sim

Adaptable, expressive, and convinced handiness is a universal qualification.

Creature type
Humanoid
Size
Small or Medium
Speed
30 feet
Adult lifespan
About 80–100 years

Everyday Expert

You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice and one Origin feat of your choice for which you qualify. This species-granted feat is additional to any feat from your background; follow the normal restrictions on taking a feat more than once. These choices represent the life you practiced before the portal incident.

Skill Grind 1 / Long Rest

Immediately after you fail an ability check that uses a skill or tool with which you are proficient, you can reroll the d20. You must use the new roll. Once you use this trait, you cannot use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

This rerolls the same attempt; it does not undo consequences, create a new opportunity, or let you attempt the impossible. It cannot reroll an attack roll or saving throw.

The Plumbob Flavor

A little translucent diamond floats above your head. Its color follows the mood you choose to portray. It sheds no usable light, has no physical substance, and provides no benefit or penalty to checks. It is obscured by cover and darkness normally, disappears while you are Invisible, and never reveals a hidden creature’s location. You can dim or dismiss it at will, without an action.

Other people see an emotional cue, not a lie detector. It reveals no thoughts, alignment, attraction, or hidden condition. Use ordinary Wisdom (Insight) checks to read people. A tense accountant is still allowed to be honest.

Where your other numbers come from

Under the 2024 rules, your background supplies your starting ability increases and its Origin feat. Your class supplies Hit Points, saving throw proficiencies, equipment training, and class features. This species adds only the traits above.

Use the campaign’s normal language choices. You may choose Simlish in place of one language if the DM allows it. Sims can learn other languages, and translation magic works normally.

An official route

For a campaign without homebrew species, use the 2024 Human with its normal traits, and add the cosmetic plumbob. Use Human mechanics in full; do not add Everyday Expert or Skill Grind.

For a 2014 campaign, use that edition’s Human and character creation rules. The 2024 background increases do not stack with 2014 species increases.

Aspirations are goals, not alignments

Choose one. It grants no ability increases or feat. At the end of an adventure, review a concrete milestone with the DM. Completing it can earn the campaign’s usual inspiration award, at most once per session; repeated chores do not qualify.

Choose an aspiration
AspirationLong-term goalExample milestoneThe vibe
LoveBuild a relationship through trust.Write an honest letter; respect the reply.Romance is a conversation, not a saving throw.
FortuneSecure a home or fund a shared project.Earn money without selling out the party.Your spreadsheet has a tab called dragons.
KnowledgeResolve a question that matters.Recover evidence and share a discovery.You label the cursed jars.
AthleticMaster a demanding physical challenge.Win fairly or help someone train.Leg day survives planar travel.
PopularityBring people together.Reconcile a dispute or host a gathering.The guest list includes the lich.
NatureProtect a living place.Restore a garden or defend a habitat.Yes, you may name the fern.
MischiefOutwit someone who deserves it.Expose a fraud without hurting bystanders.The prank budget excludes arson.
CreativityMake something people will remember.Finish and share an original work.The dungeon does need better lighting.

Life stages, without the countdown

The Neighborhood’s accelerated birthdays are a storytelling conceit. In this adaptation, Sims age at a human pace. Young adult, adult, and elder adventurers use the same statistics. Age grants no automatic ability bonuses, penalties, or daily death saves.

Infant, toddler, child, and teen stages are useful for family stories and NPCs; they are not alternate combat packages. If rapid aging is central to a particular story, settle its pace and endpoint together before play. A birthday cake cannot grant levels.

Personality that produces choices

Choose two traits and interpret them as tendencies you can act on. A trait is most useful when it creates both a temptation and a constructive contribution. It should give the player something to choose, rather than instruct the DM to seize control of the character.

Personality prompts
TraitWhat tempts youHow it helps the party
PerfectionistDelay until every detail is right.Notice a weak seam, prepare carefully, and decide when “good enough” protects people.
OutgoingFill every silence.Introduce companions, include a quiet NPC, or ask the question nobody else will.
LonerRetreat when conversation becomes tiring.Respect another person’s boundaries and offer calm companionship without a performance.
AmbitiousTreat every task as a test of your worth.Turn a vague goal into a practical plan and recognize somebody else’s achievement.
ClumsyExpect the worst from your coordination.Prepare for mishaps with ropes, padding, and a willingness to laugh at a safe mistake. No automatic failed rolls.
NeatTry to control an untidy environment.Maintain the supplies, find an item in the emergency bag, or notice that something was disturbed.
Hot-headedRespond before you have all the facts.Name the injustice clearly, then choose a response your companions can support.
CreativeStart another project before finishing the first.See an unusual use for ordinary equipment and invite the DM to adjudicate a concrete idea.

Give your Sim five anchors

Write a sentence for each: a person they trust, a place they miss, a skill they are proud of, a mistake they have not forgiven themselves for, and a hope they cannot accomplish alone. Those anchors give the DM usable hooks and give the other players reasons to care about your character.

For example, a scientist trusts the mechanic who checked their first rocket, misses a rooftop garden, takes pride in careful documentation, regrets ignoring an apprentice’s warning, and hopes to build a safe way home for everyone. None of those details needs a new resource bar. All of them can matter in play.

Relationships are remembered events

Replace a numerical friendship meter with three short notes: what you shared, what they want, and what remains unresolved. “Helped Mara save the greenhouse; she wants the missing seed ledger; she knows I lied about the accident” is more useful than “Mara: 74.” Trust grows through choices, changes with circumstances, and does not make an NPC obliged to obey.

If your Sim and another player character have a close bond, agree on what each player enjoys about it. Give the bond a practical expression—sharing a watch, checking a repair, keeping an old letter—and let it change through the story. A disagreement can make a good scene without becoming an excuse to undermine the party.

03

The everyday stuff

Big feelings. Small bookkeeping.

Keep the emotional color. Give the dice a little breathing room.

Default: choose one current mood. It has no numerical effect, imposes no condition, and never takes control of your character. Change it when the fiction changes, without spending an action.

Fine

Business as usual.

A reliable baseline. You may still have a personality.

Happy

A small thing went right.

Tell a companion what made your day.

Elated

A very large thing went right.

Celebrate. The dragon can hear you; that is ordinary sound.

Focused

One thing at a time.

Describe a checklist, a ritual, or a very serious notebook.

Inspired

An idea refuses to leave.

Sketch, compose, invent. Finish one project eventually.

Playful

The bit is going well.

Make a joke the rest of the table enjoys.

Flirty

Feeling charming.

Offer a compliment. Let the other person choose their response.

Confident

You have a plan.

Volunteer. You still roll the normal dice.

Tense

Too many things at once.

Ask for a pause or offer a small, manageable task.

Angry

Something feels unfair.

Say what upset you. You choose whether to act on it.

Sad

A loss needs space.

Lean on a bond; comfort need not fix everything.

Embarrassed

That went differently in your head.

Make a graceful exit. It will become a story, not a death save.

Moodlets are little story prompts

“Nicely fed,” “rained on,” “witnessed a loss,” and “just showered” explain a mood. They do not stack modifiers, impose Frightened, or interfere with Concentration. A frightening monster can still impose the actual Frightened condition through its printed rules; being tense cannot.

Six needs. One camp check-in.

Optional: at camp or during a meaningful break, glance at the six needs below. Mark them Satisfied, Could use attention, or Need a break. There are no timers or numerical depletion tracks. Ordinary meals, conversation, and sanitation happen offscreen unless the scene makes them relevant.

Optional needs checklist
NeedHow to meet itIf circumstances prevent it
HungerEat a normal meal; carry normal rations.Use the campaign’s food and malnutrition rules. No second Sim-specific starvation clock.
EnergyGet the sleep and rest your character requires.Use the campaign’s rest and Exhaustion rules. A nap never restores spell slots by itself.
SocialTalk, write a letter, share a quiet moment.A roleplay prompt. Solitude never forces speech, sadness, or a mechanical penalty.
FunEnjoy a hobby, a game, or a harmless bit.A roleplay prompt. Combat bonuses cannot be farmed by juggling at camp.
HygieneWash with available water and supplies.Describe grime if relevant. No poison aura, lost actions, or automatic social penalty.
BladderTake a private break when possible.Handle discreetly. No combat speed penalty or embarrassment damage.
One cause, one consequence

If lack of food already causes Exhaustion, do not add a separate mood penalty. Needs cannot cancel a rest, force PvP, or reward repetitive chores. A good camp scene can earn normal inspiration at the DM’s discretion, within the aspiration limit above.

How to run a camp scene

Use the checklist once when the group has breathing room. Ask each interested player to choose a small action and, optionally, a companion to share it with. A character who has had enough attention can simply rest; participation is not a toll required to recover resources.

  1. Establish the situation. Is the camp safe, are supplies available, and what rest is actually possible? Resolve any genuine survival problem with the campaign’s usual rules.
  2. Choose a need worth a scene. A meal, a game, a wash, or a quiet conversation can be described briefly. Skip needs that are already satisfied or uninteresting.
  3. Ask one useful question. What went well today? What frightened you? What did you learn about home? Invite an answer, not a confession.
  4. Mark the checklist manually. The fiction determines the status. A good conversation can meet Social; it cannot restore spell slots.
  5. Take the actual rest benefits. Spend Hit Dice or recover features only if the rest qualifies under the relevant rules. Keep the narrative check-in separate from that calculation.
Rain, bad soup, and a useful conversation

The group reaches shelter after a wet journey. The chef uses rations to make something warm, the Fighter repairs a strap, and the Wizard admits the portal readings do not match the map. Hunger can be marked Satisfied, and the conversation may satisfy Social. Nobody gains a universal attack bonus. The scene’s reward is a clear plan for tomorrow and the chance to know the people making it.

When a mood changes the fiction

A mood can change your description, your priorities, or the action you choose. An Angry Sim may state a boundary firmly. A Sad Sim may ask a friend to speak first. An Inspired Sim may offer an unexpected plan. The player still chooses, and the action uses its ordinary rules.

Situations may justify Advantage or Disadvantage under normal adjudication, but the reason should be a concrete circumstance: convincing evidence, credible assistance, an obstructed view, or a real condition. “My plumbob is green” is not a circumstance that makes every task easier. “I found the maintenance diagram and can explain the correct lever” might help, regardless of the plumbob’s color.

Let comfort be valuable without making it mandatory

A pleasant home can make a campaign feel generous. Give it narrative uses: a dependable meeting place, a neighbor who will receive a message, a safe cupboard for samples, or a garden somebody remembers to water. Its benefits come from established relationships and practical access, rather than an automatic increase to every saving throw.

When the party is imprisoned or lost, use the needs to describe what they miss and what small relief means to them. Avoid six parallel punishments for the same hardship. One shared cup of clean water can be an excellent scene without having to become six separate game mechanics.

04

A slightly unusual household

Different lives. The same rules budget.

Eight alternatives to the ordinary Sim, plus a sensible route into spellcasting.

Choose one replacement, not an upgrade. An occult package replaces both Everyday Expert and Skill Grind. Keep the Sim’s type, size, Speed, lifespan, and cosmetic plumbob. You gain no traits from the ordinary package and no traits from a monster with the same name.

How innate spells work

For a package with spells, you learn its cantrip at character level 1. At levels 3 and 5, you always have the listed spells prepared. Each listed leveled spell can be cast once without a spell slot, recharging on a Long Rest. You may also cast it with any spell slots you have. Use its normal casting time, range, components, duration, Concentration, and target restrictions.

Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability for this package when you select it. Your save DC is 8 + Proficiency Bonus + that ability’s modifier; your spell attack modifier is Proficiency Bonus + that modifier. The Werewolf package has no innate spells.

Mending does not restore your Hit Points. You gain no extra armor, disease immunity, condition immunity, or extra attunement. Water is not a damage type or automatic shutdown.

Spellcaster is a class choice

An ordinary Sim Wizard, Sorcerer, Bard, Druid, or other spellcaster can study in the Realm of Magic. “Spellcaster” grants no additional ancestry package, free spells, spell charges, perk points, or overcharge mechanic. Use your class’s rules.

Turning during an adventure

A bite, haunting, or strange meal can introduce a story. Changing packages takes player and DM agreement, normally at a Long Rest or between adventures. Replace the old package in full; do not collect occult traits. Already-expended daily uses stay expended until a later Long Rest. You cannot switch back and forth to refresh resources.

Balance target

These deliberately modest packages sit within a normal species budget. They give flavor, a narrow signature, and at most a cantrip plus two daily spells. Test them in your campaign; this is a revised homebrew draft, not a claim of completed playtesting. Full vampires, incorporeal ghosts, and world-shaping fairies are NPCs or the result of high-level class abilities.

Living with an unusual life

These notes add characterization and adventure hooks. They grant no powers beyond the chosen replacement package.

Vampire

The immortal aesthetic, the mortal adventure

Decide what remains ordinary about this person: a work schedule, a favorite food, a friend they have not called. Their present package still has a normal lifespan and ordinary healing; agelessness belongs to a separately agreed story, not an assumed mechanical benefit. A night-shift doctor or meticulous historian can be as compelling as an aristocrat.

A story to begin with. A plasma-fruit supplier has stopped sending letters. Finding them is about loyalty and food security, not a mandatory blood frenzy.

Mermaid

A person with two familiar worlds

Describe what moving between land and water feels like and which community taught them to do it. Their swimming and breathing are real package benefits; a magical song uses the exact listed spell. A Mermaid Bard and a Mermaid Fighter can share an origin while playing very differently.

A story to begin with. A coastal community needs help tracing a polluted current. The mermaid can scout below the surface, but needs companions to follow the problem inland.

Werewolf

A change you can choose

Choose a physical tell, a grounding habit, and a relationship to the pack. The shift is under your control. A full moon can make a reunion, ritual, or difficult memory important without forcing violence. At the table, announce when you are shifting and remember that doing so spends the Bonus Action you might otherwise need.

A story to begin with. Two packs disagree about a safe passage. Your value is understanding both sides, not winning every conversation by howling.

Ghost-touched

An echo with a future

Choose what marks the brush with death: a muted reflection, a soft glow, or a voice that seems a little distant. The body still occupies space and uses normal healing. Their unresolved business should create a goal they can pursue with the party rather than require every adventure to stop until one private problem is solved.

A story to begin with. Someone has been using the name on an old grave. The ghost-touched Sim wants to know why, and is unsure whether they want the answer.

Fairy-touched

Wonder with practical responsibilities

Decide whether the fairy influence is familiar, inherited, or newly discovered. Wings can be expressive even before any spell moves you through the air. Faerie Fire and Levitate are useful but limited; practice how they work so the colorful description makes the table clearer.

A story to begin with. A small community’s seasonal celebration has lost the person who keeps an old promise. Restoring the relationship matters more than growing a spectacular tree.

Alien

Curiosity with boundaries

Give your Alien a genuine area of ignorance and a real reason to respect the people they study. Their willing telepathic link is good for quiet cooperation, not for reading secrets. Detect Thoughts and Disguise Self introduce their own printed limits and can have social consequences when discovered.

A story to begin with. A research station has filed the party under “local wildlife.” You need to correct the record before a very earnest collector arrives.

PlantSim

Care is a two-way practice

Describe how sunlight, weather, and cultivated places affect their comfort. The package deliberately permits ordinary rations, so a long cave adventure remains possible. The body uses ordinary healing; a gardener can still ask permission before pruning anything. A PlantSim can enjoy cities without being a walking ecological lecture.

A story to begin with. An imported seed variety is displacing a local crop. The answer requires knowledge, cooperation, and a plan for the farmers who already depend on it.

Servo

A person, not an appliance

Choose who built the chassis, who chose the name, and what the Servo likes that surprises their maker. Treat autonomy as a basic fact of the character. Describe rest and food as appropriate maintenance while applying the package’s actual rules. Repairs use real healing or rest resources, even when the description involves a screwdriver.

A story to begin with. A workshop is selling replicas of your original design. The difficult question is what happens when one of the replicas asks to leave.

05

A life of useful practice

Find your calling. Learn your class.

Twelve core class guides, sixteen careers, and two worked starting characters.

Choose how you want to spend a turn. A career gives your Sim a past; a D&D class gives them the actions, resources, and progression they use on an adventure. The guides below help you connect the two. They summarize the 2024 SRD classes and add play advice, not extra class features.

Start with the activity you enjoy: protecting people, solving a tactical puzzle, investigating, performing, or exploring. Then choose a class whose ordinary turn supports that activity. A scientist can be a meticulous Wizard, an intuitive Sorcerer, or a martial researcher with no spellcasting at all. You do not have to match a job title to one compulsory build.

All milestone levels below are levels in that class. Multiclassing can delay them. These are guided routes, not substitutes for the full feature text, spell lists, equipment choices, or subclass rules in the SRD class chapter.

Class guidesCareer pathsStarting characters
Choose by play style
I want to…Good starting classesWhat I will manage
Stand between danger and the partyFighter, Paladin, BarbarianPosition, attacks, defenses, and limited bursts.
Move quickly and solve precise problemsRogue, Monk, RangerMovement, qualifying attacks, and a few tactical resources.
Help allies and shape conversationsBard, ClericSupport choices, spell preparation, and Concentration.
Investigate and change the battlefieldWizard, DruidA varied spell toolkit and the right answer for the situation.
Customize a strong magical identitySorcerer, WarlockA focused spell plan, points or Pact slots, and distinctive choices.

Twelve ways to be an adventurer

The abilities and Hit Dice listed here describe the class. Choose skills, training, and equipment from its actual starting options. Your species, background, and class each contribute once.

BarbarianBardClericDruidFighterMonkPaladinRangerRogueSorcererWarlockWizard

The neighborhood powerhouse

Barbarian

Durable melee pressure

Some Sims find peace in a garden. You find it in lifting the garden shed. A Barbarian can be a competitive athlete, a demolition worker, a protective parent, or a werewolf who has learned to direct their strength. The class is about endurance and commitment; your character can be patient, articulate, and extremely good with children.

Ability priorities
Strength; then Constitution and Dexterity
Hit Die
d12
Saving throws
Strength, Constitution

Your mechanical engine

Rage is a Bonus Action feature with limited uses. It provides its printed damage benefits and defenses; an Angry mood does not activate it. Reckless Attack, gained at level 2, trades defensive safety for offensive reliability. Your decision is when that exchange helps the party. You cannot cast spells or maintain Concentration while raging.

Barbarian progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Rage, Unarmored Defense, Weapon Mastery; then Danger Sense and Reckless Attack.Learn which attacks use Strength and what keeps Rage active.
3–4Choose a subclass at 3; the Berserker is the SRD option. Primal Knowledge expands your practical competence.Decide whether to improve your main ability or choose an eligible feat at 4.
5–10Extra Attack and Fast Movement arrive at 5; Brutal Strike arrives at 9.Your job grows from hitting hard to controlling where opponents can stand.
11–16Relentless Rage, improved Brutal Strike, and Persistent Rage improve staying power.Protect vulnerable allies without assuming every threat deals physical damage.
17–20Further Brutal Strike improvements, Indomitable Might, an Epic Boon, and Primal Champion.Treat great strength as a way to solve ambitious problems, not to overrule the party.

A useful turn

Before charging, identify the enemy that most threatens an ally. Move into a position that makes it costly to ignore you, enter Rage if the fight merits a use, and attack. At level 5, resolve both attacks separately. Use Reckless Attack when landing a hit matters more than the retaliation it invites; against many archers, that can be an expensive bargain.

Between encounters

Choose a trained skill that gives your strong Sim an identity beyond Athletics: perhaps Nature for the gardener or Insight for the union representative. Carry practical equipment for lifting, securing, and rescuing. A rope and a good question often accomplish more than a broken door.

In play

A Rogue needs time to open the evacuation gate. You occupy the narrow approach and fight the two guards rather than chasing the fleeing captain. The successful turn is the one that buys your ally another round. “But I was winning the duel” is a poor answer to a burning building.

Keep it sensible. Rage and the Werewolf shift are separate Bonus Actions. You cannot activate both on the same turn. Temporary Hit Points from shifting do not stack with another source, and the shift does not extend Rage.

The creative professional

Bard

Support, control, and social versatility

Your work changes how people see a room. It might be music, theater, painting, storytelling, or a motivational presentation that should have been an email. A Bard turns practiced expression into magic. They need not be famous, flirtatious, or even particularly comfortable in a crowd; a quiet archivist can be a remarkable storyteller.

Ability priorities
Charisma; then Dexterity and Constitution
Hit Die
d8
Saving throws
Dexterity, Charisma

Your mechanical engine

Bardic Inspiration uses a Bonus Action to give another eligible creature a die. Its current version can be used after a failed D20 Test, within its duration. Spellcasting supplies your control and healing, while Expertise makes selected skills dependable. At level 5, Font of Inspiration improves how often you can replenish your inspiration dice.

Bard progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Spellcasting and Bardic Inspiration; Expertise and Jack of All Trades at 2.Pick a small set of social and practical skills you want to own.
3–4Choose a subclass at 3; College of Lore is the SRD option.A Lore Bard is an excellent writer, critic, researcher, or painter.
5–10Font of Inspiration at 5, Countercharm at 7, more Expertise at 9, and Magical Secrets at 10.Develop a support plan that works across multiple encounters.
11–16Higher-level spells and a growing inspiration die broaden your influence.Choose spells that answer problems the party actually encounters.
17–20Level 9 spells, Superior Inspiration, an Epic Boon, and Words of Creation.Your performances can become campaign-changing events; discuss their consequences.

A useful turn

A strong opening often combines a control spell with Bardic Inspiration for the ally about to attempt the crucial task. Later, maintain Concentration and reposition instead of spending a new slot every round. Healing Word can return a fallen ally to the action when its target and range permit it; a cantrip or a useful non-spell action may then fit the rest of your turn under the spell-slot rule.

Between encounters

Ask what an NPC wants before choosing Persuasion, Deception, or another approach. A beautiful speech cannot make a hostile faction abandon its fundamental interests. Performance can earn an audience, a meal, or a contact; agree on the opportunity and stakes rather than assuming an automatic income stream.

In play

The banquet turns into a fight. You create an opening with Faerie Fire, inspire the Fighter, and move behind a solid table. On the next round, you help the civilians find an exit while the spell continues. The centerpiece has finally become a productive design choice.

Keep it sensible. An instrument is a focus when your class permits it, not a source of free inspiration. Painting the same mural every morning does not grant a new die. Use the actual class feature and track its uses.

Full Bard rules · SRD p. 31 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The caregiver with a calling

Cleric

Healing, protection, and divine utility

A Sim Cleric might have been a doctor, a community chaplain, a mortuary attendant, or the one neighbor everybody trusted during an emergency. Their divine relationship gives meaning to care. It can be sincere, questioning, practical, or complicated. The plumbob is not a hotline to a deity; you still have to decide what you believe.

Ability priorities
Wisdom; then Constitution and an armor-appropriate physical ability
Hit Die
d8
Saving throws
Wisdom, Charisma

Your mechanical engine

Prepared divine spells let you adjust to the coming day. Divine Order defines part of your starting approach, and Channel Divinity arrives at level 2. The Life Domain is a focused healing option when subclasses arrive at 3. Your party benefits from prevention and control as well as from restoring Hit Points.

Cleric progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Spellcasting and Divine Order; then Channel Divinity.Choose an order that fits whether you expect to stand in armor or emphasize magical knowledge.
3–4Choose a domain at 3; Life Domain is available in the SRD.Keep both an emergency healing option and a way to influence the fight.
5–10Level 3 spells and Sear Undead at 5, Blessed Strikes at 7, Divine Intervention at 10.Resurrection-related spells still require their actual components and eligible targets.
11–16Higher-level spells and Improved Blessed Strikes broaden your contribution.Prepare for curses, dangerous journeys, and recovery after major battles.
17–20Level 9 spells, late domain features, an Epic Boon, and Greater Divine Intervention.Miracles can resolve crises; they do not eliminate the story’s need for judgment.

A useful turn

Decide whether the urgent problem is incoming damage, a dangerous condition, or an ally already down. Bless can help several companions succeed, but occupies Concentration. A damaging cantrip or the Dodge action can be a good follow-up while that support continues. Save a healing option for an emergency instead of feeling obliged to refill every scratch during combat.

Between encounters

Build relationships with temples, clinics, and people who cannot pay. A mundane diagnosis may use Medicine; curing a magical effect uses the actual spell or feature. This distinction gives your doctor worthwhile scenes even on days when their greatest miracle is changing a clean bandage.

In play

The Rogue falls beside the laboratory door. You restore enough Hit Points to get them moving, then take cover instead of following them into the open. After the fight, ask who has Hit Dice and what threats remain before spending every remaining spell slot. Medicine is also resource management.

Keep it sensible. Your job title does not supply a healer’s kit, extra spells, or permission to ignore costly resurrection materials. Take the equipment and proficiencies your build actually grants.

Full Cleric rules · SRD p. 36 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The keeper of inconvenient nature

Druid

Battlefield control, healing, and exploration

You understand why the garden is angry. A Druid can be a botanist, conservationist, beekeeper, village herbalist, or person who tried composting once and never stopped. Their connection to nature can include cities, cultivated land, and carefully repaired ecosystems. A PlantSim is one possible appearance, not a requirement.

Ability priorities
Wisdom; then Constitution and Dexterity
Hit Die
d8
Saving throws
Intelligence, Wisdom

Your mechanical engine

Spellcasting is available from level 1. Primal Order shapes your approach, and Wild Shape and Wild Companion arrive at level 2. Use the actual allowed forms, limits, and resource rules. Circle of the Land, available at level 3, suits a Sim whose magic grows from places, seasons, and practical ecological knowledge.

Druid progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Spellcasting, Druidic, and Primal Order; then Wild Shape and Wild Companion.Prepare control, healing, and an exploration answer rather than only damage.
3–4Choose a circle at 3; Circle of the Land is the SRD option.Know what your Beast forms can do before a tense scene begins.
5–10Level 3 spells and Wild Resurgence at 5, Elemental Fury at 7, later circle features.Think about where allies can move through your terrain effects.
11–16Higher-level spells and Improved Elemental Fury extend your reach.Weather, travel, and restoration become major parts of your toolkit.
17–20Level 9 spells, Beast Spells, an Epic Boon, and Archdruid.Large ecological changes deserve large conversations about the setting.

A useful turn

Use terrain to change the problem. Entangle can hold an approach while the party deals with another enemy. Once concentrating, choose a safe position and a sustainable action. Wild Shape is a tool, not an automatic best choice every round: changing form, maintaining a spell, and keeping an ally alive may compete for your attention.

Between encounters

Ask how a place functions: water, soil, pests, shelter, local knowledge. Speak with Animals can supply a viewpoint, but an animal knows what it has experienced, not the villain’s complete plan. Gardening becomes satisfying when you help a community solve an actual problem rather than instantly filling every field with treasure.

In play

Two guards are pursuing your companions through the greenhouse. You obstruct their route and point out a clear path for the party. The vines are the spell’s effect; they do not also become harvestable magical fruit or make your Cowplant friendly. Ecology has paperwork too.

Keep it sensible. Photosynthesis is a PlantSim species trait only if you chose that package. A Druid’s class does not change their creature type, eliminate food, or let Mending heal them.

Full Druid rules · SRD p. 41 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The reliable professional

Fighter

Consistent weapon damage and adaptable defense

Your Sim practiced until the motion became dependable. That could mean competitive sport, security work, military service, historical fencing, or a lifetime of protecting a household. The Fighter is a natural choice when you want your turn to be clear while leaving room for personality and decisions. Simple mechanics do not require a simple character.

Ability priorities
Strength or Dexterity; then Constitution
Hit Die
d10
Saving throws
Strength, Constitution

Your mechanical engine

Fighting Style, Second Wind, and Weapon Mastery establish your approach at level 1. Action Surge at 2 is a limited burst of action economy; its extra action cannot be the Magic action. Tactical Mind lets the same stamina resource support certain failed ability checks. These features make a Fighter useful between fights as well as in them.

Fighter progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Fighting Style, Second Wind, Weapon Mastery; then Action Surge and Tactical Mind.Choose weapons whose mastery properties you understand.
3–4Choose a subclass at 3; Champion is the SRD option.Match your feat or ability improvement to your weapon and defense plan.
5–10Extra Attack and Tactical Shift at 5; later Indomitable and Tactical Master.Decide whether a burst now prevents more trouble than saving it.
11–16Three attacks with the Attack action at 11, Studied Attacks at 13, and further feat opportunities.Adapt weapon choices to enemies instead of defaulting to the largest damage die.
17–20More Action Surge and Indomitable uses, an Epic Boon, and four attacks with the Attack action at 20.You remain the person who can keep doing useful work when spell slots are low.

A useful turn

Get into a useful position, choose a target, and resolve attacks and mastery effects in order. At level 5, Extra Attack means two attacks when you take the Attack action; it does not give you two actions. Action Surge can provide another permitted action. Second Wind uses your Bonus Action, so plan around any other feature that needs it.

Between encounters

Take a skill that reflects what you did before adventuring. A military Sim might know History or Survival; a famous athlete might learn Persuasion. Training, equipment maintenance, and giving another character a credible Help action are ways to stay present in quieter scenes.

In play

A guard is holding the bridge. Your weapon’s actual mastery effect makes an opening, and you move so the Wizard can cross safely. You save Action Surge until the enemy officer appears. Later, Tactical Mind helps with the damaged winch, subject to its rules. Strength has a non-combat job again.

Keep it sensible. An ironing board does not inherit a martial weapon’s reach or mastery by appearance alone. If the DM approves it as a full reskin of an existing weapon, use that weapon’s entire rules package.

Full Fighter rules · SRD p. 47 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The wellness expert who can actually fight

Monk

Mobile melee pressure and tactical disruption

Your routine has finally become supernatural. A Monk may have taught fitness, practiced dance, trained for competition, or maintained a quiet spiritual discipline. They are not required to be austere. A Sim who loves comfortable furniture can still have extraordinary control over their body; they just complain during the floor exercises.

Ability priorities
Dexterity and Wisdom; then Constitution
Hit Die
d8
Saving throws
Strength, Dexterity

Your mechanical engine

Martial Arts supports Dexterity-based fighting and an Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action under its conditions. Monk’s Focus arrives at level 2 and fuels enhanced maneuvers. Focus Points are a class resource, distinct from the Focused mood. The class rewards choosing when to close, when to disengage, and when to spend points on pressure or defense.

Monk progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Martial Arts and Unarmored Defense; then Focus, mobility, and Uncanny Metabolism.Learn the free and Focus-powered versions of your mobility options.
3–4Deflect Attacks and a subclass at 3; Slow Fall and a feat opportunity at 4.Warrior of the Open Hand is the SRD subclass.
5–10Extra Attack and Stunning Strike at 5; later Evasion and Heightened Focus.Use disruption on a target your allies can exploit.
11–16Stronger martial arts, Deflect Energy, Disciplined Survivor, and Perfect Focus.Your defenses improve; deliberate positioning still matters.
17–20Late subclass abilities, Superior Defense, an Epic Boon, and Body and Mind.Your reliability comes from the class progression, not from a permanent mood bonus.

A useful turn

A mobile turn is a sequence, not a race. Find a target you can reach without stranding yourself, take the Attack action, and choose a Bonus Action that supports the situation. Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind serve different needs. Spending points on damage while surrounded may leave a very impressive corpse.

Between encounters

Discipline supports an engaging personality: what do you practice, who taught you, and what interrupts your routine? Acrobatics, Insight, and practical training scenes can make your Sim valuable during negotiations or travel. A calming exercise can meet a need narratively without granting free healing.

In play

An enemy caster is beyond the front line. You move along the side, attack, and use a legal disruption option. If you cannot safely stay there, use your remaining movement and the appropriate mobility feature to withdraw. Your party’s follow-up is part of the plan; tell them what opening you are creating.

Keep it sensible. Armor or a Shield can turn off important Monk benefits. A Vampire bite or Werewolf claw does not grant additional attacks, and using another damage option does not add two separate damage formulas together.

Full Monk rules · SRD p. 49 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The household’s sworn protector

Paladin

Armored defense, burst damage, and support

You have made a promise and intend to keep it. Your Sim might be a firefighter, bodyguard, officer, neighborhood organizer, or survivor who decided nobody else should face the same danger alone. Their oath supplies values worth testing. The interesting question is often how to keep a promise when two good obligations conflict.

Ability priorities
Strength and Charisma; then Constitution
Hit Die
d10
Saving throws
Wisdom, Charisma

Your mechanical engine

Lay On Hands, Spellcasting, and Weapon Mastery start at level 1. Fighting Style and Paladin’s Smite arrive at 2. In the 2024 rules, Divine Smite is a spell with its own Bonus Action timing and limits. Your aura at level 6 turns positioning into a party-wide concern rather than a private damage calculation.

Paladin progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Healing pool, spells, mastery; then Fighting Style and Paladin’s Smite.Keep a clear distinction between healing, spell slots, and your Bonus Action.
3–4Channel Divinity and an oath at 3.Oath of Devotion is the SRD option; write a vow your character can explain.
5–10Extra Attack and Faithful Steed at 5; Aura of Protection at 6; later Abjure Foes and Aura of Courage.Stand where the aura helps without placing the whole party in one hazard.
11–16Radiant Strikes, higher spells, Restoring Touch, and later oath features.Support and reliable weapon attacks remain useful even when you do not smite.
17–20Higher spell access, Aura Expansion at 18, an Epic Boon, and the oath’s capstone.Your reputation becomes a resource the story can challenge.

A useful turn

Choose between a support spell, straightforward attacks, and a smite opportunity. At level 5, two attacks do not mean two Bonus Actions. If you spend that Bonus Action on Lay On Hands, you cannot also spend it on Divine Smite that turn. A moderate hit that keeps the party standing can be better than a spectacular hit that empties your reserves.

Between encounters

Give your protector a relationship to authority. Do they work within institutions, challenge them, or distrust the person who signed their old employment contract? Persuasion, Insight, and Medicine can make a Paladin more than the person who asks every stranger to justify their alignment.

In play

The team is crossing a room full of hostile magic. You remain near the most vulnerable companions so your actual aura can help. When an ally falls, you decide whether to heal or finish the enemy threatening them. The oath is expressed through a choice, not through a compulsory speech.

Keep it sensible. The Love aspiration does not add Charisma or alter your aura. A career in security does not grant a second Fighting Style. Use only the benefits your chosen features provide.

Full Paladin rules · SRD p. 53 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The guide who packed properly

Ranger

Weapon pressure, scouting, and practical magic

You are the Sim who checked the weather, bought the rope, and noticed the trail was wrong. A Ranger might have been a conservationist, detective, ranch hand, explorer, or astronaut working far beyond their original training. Their expertise can be urban or rural. Knowing a city’s service passages is as useful as knowing a woodland path.

Ability priorities
Dexterity and Wisdom; then Constitution
Hit Die
d10
Saving throws
Strength, Dexterity

Your mechanical engine

Spellcasting, Favored Enemy, and Weapon Mastery start at level 1. Favored Enemy supplies its own access to Hunter’s Mark and limited free casts; the spell still requires Concentration. Deft Explorer and Fighting Style arrive at level 2. Choose whether your magic supports damage, control, healing, or investigation in the situation at hand.

Ranger progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Spells, Favored Enemy, mastery; then Deft Explorer and Fighting Style.An Expertise choice can anchor your investigative identity.
3–4Choose a subclass at 3; Hunter is the SRD option.Prepare a travel or control spell as well as a damage plan.
5–10Extra Attack at 5, Roving at 6, more Expertise at 9, and Tireless at 10.Scouting improves when you also know how to bring the party along.
11–16Later subclass features, Relentless Hunter, Nature’s Veil, and higher spells.Your mark improves through actual features, not through a second occult rank.
17–20Precise Hunter, Feral Senses, an Epic Boon, and Foe Slayer.Track a changing world; powerful senses are still bounded by their printed range.

A useful turn

Before applying Hunter’s Mark, decide whether another Concentration spell would do more for this encounter. A restrained enemy, a healed ally, or a safer retreat may matter more than extra damage. Use cover, range, and the mastery properties you actually selected. A Ranger who remains standing can keep contributing over a long day.

Between encounters

Ask specific scouting questions: where are the exits, what made these tracks, and how recent is the disturbance? Tell the DM how you search. Expertise improves a check, but it does not make every clue automatically visible or every trail readable through solid stone.

In play

You identify the guards’ patrol route, then guide the group to cover rather than walking ahead until combat starts alone. When the fight begins, you target the guard threatening the party’s escape. Your exploration work made the fight easier before anyone rolled Initiative.

Keep it sensible. Hunter’s Mark competes with other Concentration spells. Recasting it may compete for your Bonus Action. A Werewolf shift, a two-weapon option, and the mark cannot all use the same Bonus Action.

Full Ranger rules · SRD p. 57 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The specialist with plausible deniability

Rogue

Precision damage and dependable skills

You know where a little precision makes a large difference. A Rogue can be a burglar, chef, detective, stage technician, courier, or caretaker who learned to work around bad institutions. The class does not require stealing from the party. A professional who respects their teammates usually survives long enough to become interesting.

Ability priorities
Dexterity; then Constitution and a concept-relevant mental ability
Hit Die
d8
Saving throws
Dexterity, Intelligence

Your mechanical engine

Sneak Attack rewards a qualifying Finesse or Ranged weapon attack and the required tactical setup. It is once per turn, not on every hit. Expertise makes selected proficiencies exceptionally reliable. Cunning Action at level 2 lets you use a Bonus Action to reposition or attempt to Hide under the normal hiding rules.

Rogue progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Expertise, Sneak Attack, Thieves’ Cant, mastery; then Cunning Action.Know how an ally near your target can help you qualify for Sneak Attack.
3–4A subclass and Steady Aim at 3.Thief is the SRD option; inspect Fast Hands before planning item combinations.
5–10Cunning Strike and Uncanny Dodge at 5; more Expertise at 6; Evasion and Reliable Talent at 7.Trade damage dice for a Cunning Strike effect when its tactical value is worth the cost.
11–16Improved Cunning Strike, Devious Strikes, Slippery Mind, and later subclass abilities.Your choices become more flexible while your skill identity stays dependable.
17–20Late subclass features, Elusive, an Epic Boon, and Stroke of Luck.Be the expert who opens possibilities for others, not the one who plays every scene alone.

A useful turn

Choose a target whose positioning lets you qualify for Sneak Attack, make your attack, and use movement and Cunning Action to avoid an unnecessary counterattack. Hiding requires a legitimate place to hide and a successful check; saying “I hide” does not create cover. If an Opportunity Attack occurs outside your own turn, Sneak Attack may apply again if all its requirements are met.

Between encounters

Name a specialty and a limit. The detective studies testimony but struggles with status; the chef reads ingredients but distrusts nobility. Expertise in Investigation or Insight provides a strong foundation, while Skill Grind can rescue a failed proficient check if you chose ordinary Sim.

In play

The Fighter engages a guard beside the emergency gate. You make a qualifying ranged attack from cover, then shift to a position where you can reach the lock next round. If the party needs the gate open more than it needs another hit, using your action on the lock can be the right contribution.

Keep it sensible. A cosmetic SimRay is not a Ranged weapon. Sneak Attack cannot be added to an ordinary spell attack or to a Vampire bite merely because the description is sneaky.

Full Rogue rules · SRD p. 61 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The person magic happened to

Sorcerer

Flexible spellcasting with focused specialization

The portal did something to you. Perhaps your family always had strange birthdays, your plumbob has started humming, or a lab experiment worked more successfully than anyone intended. A Sorcerer’s relationship to magic is personal rather than academic. Decide whether your Sim treats that power as a gift, an inconvenience, or a skill they are determined to master.

Ability priorities
Charisma; then Constitution and Dexterity
Hit Die
d6
Saving throws
Constitution, Charisma

Your mechanical engine

Spellcasting and Innate Sorcery start at level 1. Font of Magic and Metamagic arrive at level 2. Sorcery Points are a limited resource used for specific transformations of spellcasting, not general permission to rewrite a spell. Pick options that support a coherent plan and read each option’s restrictions.

Sorcerer progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Spells and Innate Sorcery; then Sorcery Points and Metamagic.Practice a dependable cantrip and one useful defensive response.
3–4Choose a subclass at 3; Draconic Sorcery is the SRD option.Explain the draconic influence as an actual part of your story, even if your career was ordinary.
5–10Level 3 spells, Sorcerous Restoration, Sorcery Incarnate at 7, and more Metamagic at 10.Spend points where they change an important outcome.
11–16Higher spells, later subclass powers, and more points expand your options.Keep both a sustainable turn and an emergency plan.
17–20Level 9 spells, more Metamagic, an Epic Boon, and Arcane Apotheosis.Choose a signature style without narrowing every answer to one damage type.

A useful turn

Pick the encounter’s priority, activate Innate Sorcery if it is worth a use, and cast a spell that addresses that priority. On later turns, preserve an effective Concentration spell and use a cantrip where appropriate. Quickened Spell changes action timing; it does not remove the 2024 limit on expending spell slots to cast spells during a turn.

Between encounters

Give your power some habits: static in your hair, a rehearsed grounding exercise, or a family member who sends unsolicited advice. These details can motivate social and research scenes. They have no automatic effect on a spell’s visibility, components, or school.

In play

Your first instinct is to throw another fire spell at the burning laboratory. Instead, you use movement and a control spell to get the trapped workers out. The dramatic glow can stay. Good judgment is a character development milestone, even if there is no notification sound.

Keep it sensible. The Focused and Inspired moods do not replenish Sorcery Points. Species spells use the ability selected for that package, which may differ from Charisma unless you deliberately matched them.

Full Sorcerer rules · SRD p. 64 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The independent contractor

Warlock

Reliable magical pressure and customized utility

Someone offered your Sim an opportunity with alarming terms. A Warlock might be a politician, performer, researcher, or person who clicked “accept” without reading the final page. The patron can be distant, curious, manipulative, or genuinely fond of them. Agree with the DM on how that relationship creates story without turning every session into an involuntary job assignment.

Ability priorities
Charisma; then Constitution and Dexterity
Hit Die
d8
Saving throws
Wisdom, Charisma

Your mechanical engine

Eldritch Invocations and Pact Magic begin at level 1. Pact slots are few, use their listed slot level, and return on a Short or Long Rest. Invocations customize your approach and have prerequisites. Magical Cunning arrives at 2; your actual patron subclass arrives at 3. A cantrip-focused plan helps you contribute between major casts.

Warlock progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Pact Magic and one invocation; then more invocations and Magical Cunning.Choose an invocation that matters to your intended play style.
3–4Choose a patron subclass at 3; Fiend Patron is the SRD option.A pact’s narrative relationship can begin earlier than the subclass mechanics.
5–10Stronger Pact slots and more invocations; Contact Patron at 9.Each short-rest opportunity becomes a party planning question.
11–16Mystic Arcanum grants specific higher-level magic separately from Pact slots.Track each Arcanum’s use separately; it is not another Pact slot.
17–20Level 9 Arcanum, further invocations, an Epic Boon, and Eldritch Master.You have learned to negotiate from a much stronger position.

A useful turn

Use a major spell when its continuing effect or immediate impact justifies a Pact slot, then rely on your chosen attack and utility options. Eldritch Blast is a common foundation, with eligible invocations shaping its role. If you selected a weapon-focused pact, plan around that actual feature instead. A short spell list rewards knowing each spell well.

Between encounters

Define what your patron wants in concrete terms: a recovered name, a protected grove, a public performance, a particular document. Give the party reasons to care about the same objective. Contacts and persuasion can drive scenes without implying supernatural coercion every time you speak.

In play

The fight begins while negotiations are still happening. You use a control spell to separate the dangerous spokesperson from their guards, then keep pressure on the route the party needs. Afterward, you ask whether there is time for a safe Short Rest. You do not declare one while the building is actively collapsing.

Keep it sensible. Pact of the Tome is an invocation, not a subclass. A sinister business card does not grant free Charm Person, and acquiring a Vampire package does not add another spell-slot progression.

Full Warlock rules · SRD p. 70 ↗Back to class choices ↑

The researcher with a field notebook

Wizard

Broad utility and prepared battlefield control

You have a hypothesis, three labeled samples, and a plan somebody should inspect. Wizards fit scientists, writers, programmers, historians, and laboratory engineers. Their spellbook can look like a technical manual or research diary while remaining a real spellbook. The important fantasy is learning and preparation, not an automatic claim to know everything.

Ability priorities
Intelligence; then Constitution and Dexterity
Hit Die
d6
Saving throws
Intelligence, Wisdom

Your mechanical engine

Your spellbook, prepared spells, ritual casting, and spell slots are different parts of your toolkit. A spell can be in the book without being prepared for ordinary casting. Ritual Adept provides its specific ritual exception. Arcane Recovery offers a limited way to regain slots during a Short Rest; it is not a full recharge whenever you sit down.

Wizard progression guide
Class levelsMilestonesYour practical decision
1–2Spellcasting, Ritual Adept, Arcane Recovery; then Scholar.Maintain a short prepared-spell list you can explain without opening six tabs.
3–4Choose a subclass at 3; Evoker is the SRD option.Your specialization adds actual features at its stated levels.
5–10Level 3 spells and Memorize Spell at 5; later subclass features and stronger spell levels.Keep a mix of control, defense, information, and damage.
11–16High-level spells increasingly change travel and problem-solving.Allow the rest of the party to contribute to the plan those spells enable.
17–20Level 9 spells, Spell Mastery at 18, an Epic Boon, and Signature Spells at 20.Powerful magic still has targets, costs, and consequences.

A useful turn

A useful opening changes the enemy’s options: block a route, hinder a group, or protect an ally. Once concentrating on something valuable, move to cover and use a cantrip or another permitted action. Shield can be an excellent Reaction when its trigger occurs, but using it spends a slot that may be needed later. Read the actual incoming threat before committing resources.

Between encounters

Ask a specific research question and identify a method. Copying a new spell takes the class’s actual time and gold, while ordinary research can involve libraries, witnesses, and experiments. Failed experiments can reveal useful clues without granting magic-item upgrades or free copies of valuables.

In play

You prepared Grease because the old mill has a narrow stair. In the fight, it makes that stair difficult to hold. Outside the fight, Detect Magic from your spellbook helps examine a device through the ritual rules. The spell reveals what it actually says; you still investigate who built the machine.

Keep it sensible. A spell’s Sims name does not grant access to it. Transportalate is still Misty Step, with its normal distance and casting details. The prototype SimRay focus in your pocket casts no extra rays by itself.

Full Wizard rules · SRD p. 77 ↗Back to class choices ↑

Sixteen careers, with room to grow

Use these as character concepts and development plans. They do not grant a separate career level, salary, spell list, or resource pool. A milestone means your character has accomplished something in the fiction; class levels still arrive through the campaign’s usual advancement.

ScientistPainterChefAthleteWriterMusicianProgrammerDetectiveCriminalDoctorAstronautActorGardenerPoliticianMilitary / securityRobotics engineer
ScientistWizard → Evoker

Starting direction. Sage; Intelligence first.

Your route into adventuring

Keep a reproducible notebook and a plan for the next experiment. At level 1, use a practical control spell such as Grease alongside a dependable cantrip; learn to preserve your limited slots. At 3, Evoker gives the laboratory a clear specialization, and at 5 your first level 3 spells make the research genuinely hazardous.

Build choices that matter

An ordinary Sim’s extra Origin feat can be Skilled for laboratory tools and another skill. An Alien package instead offers its own mental and disguise abilities; it replaces the ordinary traits.

A life between levels

During downtime, find a collaborator, recover a component, or test one bounded hypothesis. Your long-term project could be a safe portal home. The recurring complication is whether it works before the grant expires.

PainterBard → College of Lore

Starting direction. Charisma; painter’s supplies from a legal proficiency choice.

Your route into adventuring

Treat spell visuals as deliberate composition: a wash of color, an ink gesture, a sketch that briefly moves. Bardic Inspiration might be a quick portrait that helps a companion see themselves clearly. At 3, Lore supports the observational side of art; your broader spell access later reflects a growing visual vocabulary.

Build choices that matter

Choose Expertise that supports your artist’s work, such as Performance or Investigation if proficient. The tools are for actual painting, while your spellcasting focus remains one your features permit.

A life between levels

Offer a portrait in exchange for a conversation, document a vanished landscape, or argue about an honest commission. Your recurring challenge is completing something while the party keeps discovering dramatic lighting.

ChefRogue → Thief

Starting direction. Dexterity; cook’s utensils through background, Skilled, or training.

Your route into adventuring

A chef’s precision transfers cleanly to Rogue: steady hands, quick movement, and a ruthless awareness of timing. Use a real Finesse weapon for attacks, describing it as a culinary knife only when the weapon’s complete statistics remain intact. Thief’s Fast Hands supports appropriate item use; it does not make every kitchen object a Bonus Action.

Build choices that matter

Choose an ordinary Sim with Skilled if you want cook’s utensils alongside practical skills. Take Medicine or Insight through a permitted choice for a caregiver or head-chef interpretation.

A life between levels

At camp, cook from the party’s supplies and ask what a meal means to someone. A famous recipe, an ethical supplier, or a restaurant destroyed in the planar incident can become a real adventure. Bard is an alternative if magical hospitality is the central fantasy.

AthleteFighter → Champion; Monk is an alternative

Starting direction. Strength or Dexterity; Soldier is an easy background route.

Your route into adventuring

Champion suits dependable physical excellence and uncomplicated turns. Fighter mastery choices can reflect a competitive discipline, and Second Wind represents trained reserves. At level 5, Extra Attack makes the routine noticeably more effective. Choose Monk instead if movement, unarmed technique, and a resource-based martial rhythm are what you want to play.

Build choices that matter

An ordinary Sim keeps the broad training and extra Origin feat. A Werewolf athlete trades those for the shift package and needs to plan its Bonus Action alongside other features.

A life between levels

Give the athlete a rival, an injury they learned from, and a reason to compete beyond winning. Teach a companion a drill or organize a local event. They may own three protein powders; none of them replaces rations.

WriterWizard → Evoker, or Bard → College of Lore

Starting direction. Intelligence for studied magic; Charisma for oral storytelling.

Your route into adventuring

Choose Wizard if the manuscript is a spellbook and investigation is your pleasure. Choose Bard if the act of telling a story changes how people feel and work together. Both routes can support a published novelist. At 3, select the actual subclass; avoid combining both progressions just because you have written dialogue and footnotes.

Build choices that matter

Useful trained skills include History, Investigation, and Performance. Choose the ones your build supplies rather than giving yourself everything a successful author might plausibly know.

A life between levels

Keep a recurring subject: the expedition’s mistakes, planar customs, or an unreliable history of the Neighborhood. A manuscript can open doors or upset a powerful reader. It cannot rewrite an NPC’s choices because the next chapter would be better that way.

MusicianBard → College of Lore

Starting direction. Charisma; use the class’s instrument proficiencies.

Your route into adventuring

Pick an instrument you can transport, tune, and explain in a dungeon. Your core turn is still a spell or other action, with Bardic Inspiration when appropriate. Lore supports the musician who collects songs and local histories. The party does not need a solo at every initiative count; establish what the magic sounds like in one good sentence.

Build choices that matter

Expertise in Performance makes the craft dependable; another choice such as Insight or Persuasion can define the person behind it. Spells such as Healing Word and Faerie Fire give different kinds of support.

A life between levels

Seek a lost composition, repay a teacher, or bring an instrument home from a ruined theater. Agree on realistic performance opportunities with the DM. One tavern cannot pay the same appearance fee seven times before breakfast.

ProgrammerWizard → Evoker

Starting direction. Intelligence; Sage and Investigation fit well.

Your route into adventuring

Your spellbook is a documented set of arcane procedures. Mage Hand is remote manipulation; Detect Magic is a diagnostic tool; a control spell is a carefully specified environmental change. Use these descriptions to communicate clearly, then apply the actual spell text. The setting is allowed to resist your insistence that all problems have a command line.

Build choices that matter

Scholar and permitted knowledge proficiencies support troubleshooting. A Servo programmer is a character with the Servo package, not a Construct immune to ordinary hazards.

A life between levels

Debug a portal by collecting evidence, speaking to its maker, and testing one component at a time. A failed test can supply a clue. “I hack the dragon” still needs a defined action and a rule that supports the intended result.

DetectiveRogue → Thief, or Ranger → Hunter

Starting direction. Dexterity; Intelligence or Wisdom according to specialty.

Your route into adventuring

Rogue emphasizes Expertise and access; Ranger emphasizes tracking, outdoor competence, and supporting magic. Choose a detective’s method before choosing the class: careful scene analysis, reading people, or following a trail. By levels 5–7, your real class features make that method more reliable without producing automatic truth detection.

Build choices that matter

Investigation, Insight, and Perception are useful choices when granted. An Alien may have Detect Thoughts through its package at character level 5, but the spell still has limits and cannot replace every interview.

A life between levels

Write down what you know, what you infer, and what remains unproven. Share your working theory so the party can help test it. The best clue is one that creates a decision, not one that lets you announce the whole plot.

CriminalRogue → Thief

Starting direction. Dexterity; Criminal background.

Your route into adventuring

Start with a professional reason to cooperate: the crew kept you alive, the job is shared, or you owe someone a clean beginning. Learn when Sneak Attack qualifies and how Cunning Action keeps you safe. Thief supplies practical versatility at 3; Cunning Strike at 5 lets you exchange some damage for specific tactical effects.

Build choices that matter

Choose an Expertise specialty that makes your niche clear. Stealth and Sleight of Hand make a classic burglar, while Investigation and Deception support a planner or confidence artist.

A life between levels

Use contacts to learn prices, exits, and who cannot be bribed. A wanted poster or a former partner can complicate a session without making you steal from companions. The getaway car did not survive the portal, so you now care deeply about horses.

DoctorCleric → Life Domain

Starting direction. Wisdom; Medicine and a healer’s kit where available.

Your route into adventuring

A Life Cleric turns a calling to care into actual healing magic. You begin with useful spells, gain Channel Divinity at 2, and enter the domain at 3. Learn the difference between stabilizing someone, restoring Hit Points, removing a condition, and bringing back the dead. Those are distinct problems with distinct tools.

Build choices that matter

Select Protector or Thaumaturge according to the character’s approach, using Divine Order’s real rules. An ordinary Sim can use Skilled to round out mundane clinical training.

A life between levels

Make rounds, maintain supplies, and learn which communities trust you. Sometimes the important scene is telling a patient the truth gently. Your strongest recurring hook is an obligation you cannot satisfy alone: an outbreak, a missing colleague, or a clinic cut off from aid.

AstronautRanger → Hunter, or Fighter → Champion

Starting direction. Dexterity or Strength; Survival and navigational interests.

Your route into adventuring

Use Ranger for expedition planning and a small amount of practical magic; choose Fighter for a trained specialist who relies on equipment and discipline. The rocket accident explains travel to Faerûn, not resistance to vacuum. At 5, either route improves weapon output through Extra Attack, while their support tools remain different.

Build choices that matter

Navigator’s tools or another practical proficiency can come from an appropriate legal choice. A background need not literally say “astronaut” to describe your previous career.

A life between levels

Recover flight records, identify a sky that does not match your charts, or seek a wizard who understands the portal. The party’s next journey becomes your next mission. Remember that a fantasy airship is not obliged to have a maintenance manual.

ActorBard → College of Lore

Starting direction. Charisma; Performance and a second social specialty.

Your route into adventuring

Your magic is rehearsal, timing, and understanding an audience. Start with spells that support disguise, distraction, or allies as your actual list permits. At 3, Lore can reflect years of learning voices, traditions, and stories. It is also perfectly reasonable for your famous actor to be a novice adventurer: awards do not stop arrows.

Build choices that matter

Disguise tools and social skills require actual proficiencies. Charm is not the same as a convincing performance, and neither guarantees a role or a relationship.

A life between levels

A fan can be a friend, a witness, or somebody with an unrealistic expectation. Use fame to create conversations the whole party can enter. The recurring joke works best when the actor discovers they are only famous in a plane nobody here has visited.

GardenerDruid → Circle of the Land

Starting direction. Wisdom; Nature, Survival, or herbalism where granted.

Your route into adventuring

Begin with useful growth, control, and care: Druidcraft, Entangle, and a healing option make a coherent starting theme. Wild Shape at 2 supports exploration, and the Land circle at 3 connects you to particular environments. At 5, Plant Growth is a meaningful expression of expertise, but follows the actual spell rather than instant-harvesting rare treasures.

Build choices that matter

A PlantSim is an appealing alternative package; an ordinary Sim gardener is equally valid and has broader training. Your chosen species and class each keep their separate benefits.

A life between levels

Give the garden a practical stake: food for a village, a species close to extinction, or the only specimen that may reopen the portal. Your best adventures grow from people depending on a place, not from a guaranteed 500-gp fruit harvest.

PoliticianBard → College of Lore, or Warlock → Fiend Patron

Starting direction. Charisma; Persuasion, Insight, and an actual platform.

Your route into adventuring

Bard fits the organizer whose power comes from persuasion and skilled coalition-building. Warlock fits a character with a literal supernatural backer and complicated obligations. Choose which fantasy matters. A Fiend Patron should be a real, agreed part of the story; it is not the mandatory explanation for every public official.

Build choices that matter

Select skills that help you understand and communicate with people. Social spells remain visible, limited, and potentially consequential according to their rules. A vote cannot be assumed to be a Charisma contest with one universal DC.

A life between levels

Write one policy your character genuinely believes would help, one compromise they regret, and one person they still answer letters from. Their best moment may be keeping a promise when nobody important is watching.

Military / securityFighter → Champion, or Paladin → Oath of Devotion

Starting direction. Strength; Soldier provides a clear starting background.

Your route into adventuring

Fighter emphasizes flexible training and sustained weapon work. Paladin adds an oath, healing, and auras to the protector role. Neither career demands automatic obedience to any uniform. Learn the actual defensive tools of the class and give the party a clear account of how you plan to keep them safe.

Build choices that matter

A Shield and appropriate armor are useful only when acquired and supported by training. A Paladin should plan Charisma as well as Strength, while a Fighter can concentrate more heavily on one attack ability.

A life between levels

A former unit, an unfinished rescue, or a disputed order can provide emotional depth. Treat the party as fellow decision-makers rather than a squad you command. The best briefing is one that includes the possibility that someone else has a better idea.

Robotics engineerWizard → Evoker; Artificer if the campaign includes it

Starting direction. Intelligence; tinker’s tools and Investigation.

Your route into adventuring

The fully supported SRD route is a Wizard whose magic looks like experimental engineering. Mage Hand manipulates parts; Mending repairs eligible objects; Find Familiar may be described as a little mechanical assistant using an allowed familiar’s real statistics. You do not receive a combat Servo by finishing an impressive backstory.

Build choices that matter

If the DM allows an Artificer book, choose the exact edition and subclass from that book and follow its entire progression. This handbook does not blend a remembered Artificer with 2024 Wizard features.

A life between levels

Recover a lost design, settle a question about a created person’s autonomy, or find replacement parts that are more than a shopping list. Your assistant should have a personality. Its legal movement speed is still the one on its stat block.

Build for the next session, not only the capstone

Choose a reliable action, a useful contribution outside combat, and one way to help a companion. Those three choices matter immediately. A clever level 20 combination is less useful if your first ten sessions leave you with a character you do not enjoy playing.

At level 4 and later feat opportunities, improve your main ability when attacks or save DCs are consistently letting you down, or choose an eligible feat that supports an actual play pattern. Half-feats, equipment, and party composition can affect that decision. Read the prerequisite and the entire feature before assuming a familiar name still works as it did in another edition.

*Full casters here are Bard, Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, and Wizard. This table assumes all levels are in the listed class. Warlock uses its own Pact Magic and Mystic Arcanum progression. Multiclass spell slots do not automatically grant knowledge or preparation of higher-level spells.

Party roles are agreements, not cages

Tell the other players what your Sim is good at and what assistance makes them better. A Rogue benefits from an ally near the target; a concentrating caster benefits from safer positioning; a Warlock benefits from realistic rest opportunities. Nobody needs to surrender every interesting conversation to the Bard or every investigation to the Wizard. Invite a specialist when the outcome matters and share scenes when it does not.

If you want to multiclass, write down what each level actually adds and what it delays. Check prerequisites, starting-versus-multiclass proficiencies, resource recovery, and spell preparation separately. One well-understood class is a complete character, even if the Neighborhood’s career website insists you need a side hustle.

Two complete starting directions

These examples use level 1, ordinary Sim, 27-point buy, and the 2024 backgrounds and classes. They demonstrate how to assemble the rules above. They are not additional species packages.

Mira Patch — level 1 scientist Wizard

Mira recorded the portal accident as “unexpected but repeatable.” Choose Sage, Wizard, and Knowledge. Sage supplies +2 Intelligence and +1 Constitution, Arcana, History, calligrapher’s supplies, and Magic Initiate (Wizard). Wizard skill choices are Investigation and Insight. Everyday Expert adds Perception and Skilled; Skilled adds Nature, tinker’s tools, and alchemist’s supplies.

Mira’s 27-point ability buy
