Numbers. Proficiency Bonus +2; HP 8 (6 + Constitution 2); AC 12 without protection or 15 while Mage Armor applies (13 + Dexterity 2); spell save DC 13 (8 + 2 + 3); spell attacks +5; Intelligence and Wisdom saves +5 and +3. Passive Perception is 13 (10 + Wisdom 1 + proficiency 2). Initiative is +2.

Cantrips. Take Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost from Wizard; take Mending and Prestidigitation from Sage’s Magic Initiate, choosing Intelligence for that feat. The scientific presentation changes none of their casting details.

Spellbook. Start with Detect Magic, Find Familiar, Grease, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, and Shield. Prepare Grease, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, and Shield through Wizard. Detect Magic and Find Familiar can be cast from the book through Ritual Adept when its conditions are met. Find Familiar still needs its consumed component.

Background magic. Choose Feather Fall as Magic Initiate’s level 1 spell. It is always prepared in addition to the Wizard choices, can be cast once without a slot per Long Rest, and can also use available spell slots. Track that free use separately. Mira has two level 1 Wizard spell slots, Arcane Recovery’s limited recovery, and one Skill Grind use.

Starting equipment. Use the actual Wizard and Sage equipment packages. The Wizard’s quarterstaff focus is a “prototype SimRay antenna” in appearance only. A book-shaped clipboard is still a spellbook. Additional workshop tools must be acquired; proficiency does not create the tools.

At level 2. Scholar can deepen a qualifying knowledge proficiency. At 3, choose Evoker and two new legal spellbook spells. At 5, evaluate the party’s needs before choosing level 3 spells; a control or utility option may matter as much as a larger explosion.

Dev Brisk — level 1 athlete Fighter

Dev crossed a planar rift because it looked like an obstacle-course checkpoint. Choose Soldier, Fighter, and Athletic. Soldier supplies +2 Strength and +1 Constitution, Athletics, Intimidation, a gaming-set proficiency, and Savage Attacker. Fighter skill choices are Acrobatics and Survival. Everyday Expert adds Perception and the Alert Origin feat.

Numbers. Proficiency Bonus +2; HP 12 (10 + Constitution 2); AC 18 with Chain Mail and a Shield (16 + 2); Speed 30 feet; Initiative +3 when using Alert’s proficiency benefit (Dexterity 1 + PB 2). Strength and Constitution saves are +5 and +4. Passive Perception is 13.

Combat choices. Take the Dueling Fighting Style. A one-handed Longsword attack is +5 to hit (Strength 3 + PB 2), dealing 1d8 + 5 Slashing damage (Strength 3 + Dueling 2). A Shield is not another weapon. Select Longsword and two other weapons for your three mastery choices, then read each property before the session.

Resources. Second Wind starts with two uses and heals 1d10 + 1 as a Bonus Action at this level. Recover uses according to its Short and Long Rest rules. Skill Grind can reroll one failed proficient ability check per Long Rest; it cannot reroll a missed Longsword attack. Apply Savage Attacker only as the feat permits.

Equipment and next levels. Choose the Fighter’s 155 GP starting option. Buy Chain Mail (75 GP), a Shield (10 GP), and a Longsword (15 GP), using 100 GP; spend the remaining 55 GP on adventuring supplies as desired. Take the Soldier equipment package separately. At 2, learn Action Surge and Tactical Mind. At 3, Champion is a direct fit. At 5, Extra Attack and Tactical Shift make Dev a much more flexible protector without adding a separate athlete resource bar.

06

Realm of Magic, translated

Familiar names. Actual spell rules.

Conversions, worked examples, and the practical details of using magic.

A name is not spell access. These entries translate Sims ideas into existing mechanics. A class, feat, species package, or DM-awarded item must grant the ability. These are not an extra spell list, and you cannot trade a known spell for an entry here without a rule allowing it.

The source rule governs every casting detail. Use your actual spellcasting DC; never add Proficiency Bonus to an already-complete DC. Ranks such as Apprentice or Grand Master are narrative titles, not a second advancement system. When using a 2014 spell or class option, use that version consistently with the DM’s approval.

The conversion notes are intentionally short. Keep the SRD 5.2.1 spell text or your chosen rulebook at the table for complete effects.

Read a power as a procedure

Before using a conversion, identify its source of access, available resource, casting time, valid targets, range, components, and duration. Then check Concentration and any ending conditions. A familiar Sims name is helpful shorthand only after everyone knows what rule it refers to.

Check a power before casting
QuestionWhy it mattersExample
How do I have it?A class, species package, feat, or actual item grants access.An ordinary Sim does not learn every Practical spell by choosing Knowledge.
What am I spending?Slots, innate free uses, item charges, and class resources are separate.A Mermaid’s free Charm Person use does not consume or replenish a Bard spell slot.
What part of my turn does it use?Actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions each have their own limits.A Bonus Action teleport leaves no second Bonus Action for another feature.
What holds it in place?Concentration can be disrupted and only supports one such effect at a time.Casting a new Concentration spell ends your previous one.
What does it actually change?Appearance does not add damage, range, movement, or authority.A blue Zipzap still uses the chosen Shocking Grasp rules.

Five examples you can take to the table

Repairio: a repair, not a promotion

A hinge is broken. A character who knows Mending checks whether the break fits the spell and spends its normal casting time. The spell can repair the eligible break; it does not upgrade the door, restore missing magical properties, or heal the Servo standing next to it. If danger is approaching, the time required is part of the decision. Repairio is not a free combat action because the name sounds quick.

Transportalate: one movement problem solved

A character with Misty Step sees a safe, unoccupied destination within its normal distance. They use a Bonus Action and the appropriate resource to teleport. The new location can solve a gap, obstruction, or immediate danger. It does not automatically carry a friend, double the distance at a narrative rank, or conceal the casting’s normal requirements. Tell the party where you intend to arrive before the spell creates a new rescue problem.

Infatuate: a charm with social consequences

A character with Charm Person uses that spell’s actual target, save, duration, and awareness rules. A success changes only what the spell says. The target retains their own wants and judgment; the spell supplies no romantic consent, permanent relationship, or universal obedience. An NPC who discovers magical interference may become much less interested in future cooperation. A good conversation has a different risk profile.

Chillio: describe the frost, keep the numbers

Ray of Frost provides the spell attack, damage, and Speed reduction written in that spell. You can describe a gleam of ice on a boot or a sudden winter breath. That description does not also impose Restrained or create a block of solid ice. If your actual goal is to stop a creature completely, look for a rule that does that and pay its real cost.

Dedeathify: a major decision with a real cost

The party has a dead companion, not merely a bad mood. Determine what restoration magic is available, whether the target qualifies, and which components, time limits, and consequences apply. Raise Dead and True Resurrection solve different problems. A renamed spell does not bridge that difference. Finding an appropriate caster or a dish of Ambrosia can become an adventure, with the fallen player involved in planning the outcome.

Spell slots and the shape of a turn

Under the 2024 rules, a creature can expend only one spell slot to cast spells on a turn. A free innate casting or cantrip interacts with that rule according to its actual requirements; a Bonus Action is still a limited part of the turn. Also read specific features such as Quickened Spell and Divine Smite, which can add their own restrictions or timing. Use one consistent rules version rather than combining the most generous parts of two editions.

Keep a short line on the character sheet for each separate source: “Alien Disguise Self free use,” “Wizard slots,” or “SimRay charges.” Having the same spell from two sources can be useful, but it does not merge their DCs, refresh their resources, or let one source ignore another source’s costs.

07

Inventory & horticulture

Pack the essentials. Label the fruit.

Signature equipment, workshop projects, gardens, and a shared household budget.

Magic items are DM-awarded treasure, not species features or automatic career equipment. The entries below are homebrew unless they explicitly point to an existing rule. Their rarity is a starting point for treasure placement; no item is available just because a character owns a lab.

Moodlet Solver Ray

Uncommon wand · requires attunement by a spellcaster

The wand has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges at dawn. As a Magic action, expend 1 charge and choose a willing creature you can see within 30 feet. It gains 1d6 + 2 Temporary Hit Points. This effect does not remove any condition or change a creature’s choices. The wand can also serve as an Arcane Focus.

The device makes a reassuring noise. Nobody knows if that is necessary.

SimRay

Rare wand · requires attunement by a spellcaster

The wand has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges at dawn, up to its maximum. While holding it, cast Ray of Frost (0 charges), Hold Person at level 2 (2 charges), or Polymorph at level 4 (4 charges). Ray of Frost uses your character level for its normal damage scaling. Use save DC 15 or spell attack +7, as appropriate. Use each spell’s normal casting time, targets, and Concentration; no components are required. Polymorph still transforms into a Beast.

The ethics committee finally answered the mind-control request. They said no.

Plentiful Needs Tonic

Common potion · consumable

Drink it as a Bonus Action. It provides one day’s food and water and leaves you comfortably clean. It can mark Hunger, Hygiene, and Bladder Satisfied in the optional checklist. It does not restore Hit Points, Hit Dice, spell slots, daily features, sleep, or remove Exhaustion or conditions.

All six bars on the label are marketing.

Portable Instrument

Mundane equipment

Use an ordinary instrument’s cost, weight, and rules. It functions as a spellcasting focus only if a feature lets you use it that way. Owning it grants neither proficiency nor Bardic Inspiration.

The portable piano remains a logistics problem.

Ironing Board

Mundane object · improvised weapon

Use the normal improvised weapon rules: normally 1d4 damage of a suitable type, no special reach, and no automatic proficiency. The DM may rule that a sturdy board resembles a particular existing weapon; use that weapon’s rules in full.

The wrinkle situation is now tactical.

Voidcritter Card

Mundane trinket or familiar reskin

A collectible card has no combat effect. If you can cast Find Familiar, your familiar can look like a Voidcritter while using one permitted familiar stat block and all the spell’s limits. The appearance grants no extra attacks, psychic damage, or teleport.

It has a favorite snack and strong opinions about the binder.

Death Flower

Uncommon wondrous item · consumable

When a living creature you can see within 30 feet fails a death saving throw, you can use your Reaction while holding this flower to consume it and replace that roll with a 10, making it a success. Use this before applying the failed roll’s effects, including the two failures from a natural 1. The flower does not heal or revive anyone, prevent other causes of death, or substitute for a spell component.

Grim accepts the gesture. He does not accept coupons.

Ambrosia

Legendary wondrous item · consumable · DM treasure

Over 1 hour, a creature administers this dish to the remains of a dead, non-Undead Sim. It casts Resurrection on that Sim without components, subject to all the spell’s other limits, eligibility, and return-to-life penalties. The dish is consumed. It does not reverse old age, erase curses, or create a playable ghost. A free and willing soul is required.

The quest recipe calls for angelfish, a Death Flower, and a Potion of Youth. These are story ingredients, not a reproducible crafting formula.

Good gardening, inconvenient botany

Plants as supplies and adventure hooks
PlantUse in this campaignLimit
Plasma FruitA ration reskin for a Vampire Sim.No healing, temporary HP, or bonus spell energy.
Forbidden Fruit of the PlantSimIntroduces a PlantSim transformation story.With player and DM agreement, adopt the PlantSim replacement package. A temporary story version lasts five days, then restores the original package; daily uses cannot be refreshed by switching.
DragonfruitA valuable or unusual crop at ordinary local produce prices.No 500-gp fruit or all-day saving throw buff. Magical fruit must be separately awarded treasure.
Money TreeA whimsical business or a source of plot trouble.Use the campaign’s ordinary downtime business rules and costs. No automatic currency generation, three-day maturation, or resale arbitrage.
CowplantA dangerous creature with a very convincing cake lure.Use the bestiary entry. It grants no automatic youth-harvesting economy.
The Mother PlantA contained—or escaped—adventure threat.Use the boss guidance below. Spores are encounter effects, not a permanent offscreen control of player characters.

Make equipment part of your story

Give a signature item a name, a repair history, and an owner’s habit. The Moodlet Solver Ray might make a reassuring chime your character no longer notices. The ironing board may have been carried from the first home they ever owned. These details make equipment memorable without changing its mechanics.

Separate appearance, function, and availability. A focus may look like Sim technology while retaining its ordinary function. A true SimRay has the item’s written charges and attunement. Neither item becomes available automatically because a career description mentions it. A missing part, a mentor, or a promised favor can explain how the real treasure enters the campaign.

A workshop project that can actually finish

  1. Define the result. Is this a mundane repair, a cosmetic reskin, a normal crafted item, or a new magic item the DM has agreed to award? Write that down before collecting materials.
  2. Set the requirements. Use the campaign’s crafting rules for proficiencies, tools, materials, cost, and working time. If a special quest component matters, say what makes it special.
  3. Let the expedition supply progress. Recover a design, consult a specialist, secure a safe workspace, or retrieve a component from a real location. A progress step should involve a decision, not only a purchase.
  4. Resolve the work. Make checks only where the outcome is uncertain and the consequences have been established. A failed check should have the agreed result, not an improvised permanent loss of all the party’s money.
  5. Record the finished item. Keep one clear rules entry with its action, range, charges, recovery, and attunement. Retire the workshop’s speculative notes so they do not become extra powers.
The cleaner that became an adventure

A Servo engineer wants a scrubber that helps maintain the shared house. The group agrees it will have the effects of mundane cleaning equipment, not a condition-removal aura. The missing pressure valve is held by a merchant who needs an escort. Completing that trip finishes the household project and creates a contact. A later magical version would be separately specified treasure, with its own limits.

Gardens have people attached

A useful garden needs space, water, time, and somebody to care for it while the party travels. Those requirements can be handled through normal downtime and established NPC relationships. Ask who owns the land, who knows the plants, and what a harvest means locally. An ordinary crop can matter enormously to hungry people without being sold for hundreds of gold pieces per fruit.

Give unusual plants explicit roles. Plasma Fruit solves an everyday supply problem. A Death Flower can be a cherished consumable or a named quest ingredient. The Forbidden Fruit introduces a voluntary transformation story. The Cowplant is a dangerous neighbor with a readable warning sign. Treating them differently produces better adventures than making every plant a permanent statistical upgrade.

Household money and fair expectations

Track ordinary money using the campaign’s currency. “Simoleons” can be a name your Sim uses for it, but do not introduce a second exchange rate unless the story needs one. Agree on rent, repairs, staff, and income through the game’s normal lifestyle or downtime procedures. A Money Tree can be a plot device, an eccentric business, or a reason to meet the tax collector; it is not a guaranteed infinite source of currency.

If the party shares a household fund, agree on who can spend it and for what. Make major purchases a group decision. The story should remember that a comfortable home is a shared achievement, including the person who insisted the roof needed attention before anyone bought a second piano.

08

Greetings from home

The Neighborhood is a big place.

Twenty origins, six longer setting guides, and stories to bring home.

Choose a world or roll 1d20 on this curated selection. Origin grants no proficiencies, resistance, spells, or mood bonus. These descriptions are loose setting inspiration, and the adventure hooks are invented for this adaptation.

01

Willow Creek

Porches, parks, and excellent gossip.

Hook A family letter arrives from a house that never had a mailbox.

02

Oasis Springs

Desert roads and hot afternoons.

Hook A salvage crew finds a rocket with your name on the manifest.

03

Newcrest

Empty lots and a great many plans.

Hook Someone is selling land that belongs to nobody. Yet.

04

Windenburg

Old ruins, cafés, and enthusiastic nightlife.

Hook A dance club is using a portal as a lighting effect.

05

San Myshuno

Apartment life, festivals, and rent.

Hook Your former landlord hires a planar debt collector.

06

Sulani

Island communities and ocean traditions.

Hook A shipping company has been dumping alchemical waste.

07

Forgotten Hollow

Long shadows and discreet neighbors.

Hook The community plasma-fruit garden has gone missing.

08

Glimmerbrook

Woodland paths leading to the Realm of Magic.

Hook A mentor wants a dangerous spellbook returned unopened.

09

Mt. Komorebi

Mountain trails, snow, and hot springs.

Hook An exhausted guide asks you to find a missing climber.

10

Evergreen Harbor

Industry, community projects, and repair work.

Hook A neighborhood vote is being influenced by an animated bin.

11

Britechester

Rival universities and overdue assignments.

Hook Your thesis committee has followed you across planes.

12

Henford-on-Bagley

Country markets and fiercely contested fairs.

Hook The prize pumpkin is suspiciously sentient.

13

StrangerVille

Dust, secrets, and an unusual plant problem.

Hook A sealed sample case has begun humming.

14

Del Sol Valley

Celebrity dreams and precarious careers.

Hook A publicist wants exclusive rights to the party’s next dungeon.

15

Brindleton Bay

Coastal paths and a lot of pets.

Hook A cat knows where the missing portal key is.

16

Copperdale

School stories and lakeside afternoons.

Hook An old friend needs help finding a stolen keepsake.

17

Chestnut Ridge

Ranches, horses, and long horizons.

Hook A lost horse returns with impossible flowers in its mane.

18

Moonwood Mill

Wooded roads and competing packs.

Hook Two packs ask for the same mediator on the same night.

19

Tomarang

Markets, rental homes, and close communities.

Hook A tenant discovers their flat overlaps a wizard’s pantry.

20

Sixam

Alien landscapes and very difficult travel.

Hook A research station has catalogued your party as local wildlife.

Sul sul. Communication, mostly.

Use Simlish as an ordinary campaign language. Familiar fan phrases such as sul sul for a greeting, dag dag for a farewell, and nooboo for a baby can add flavor. Do not treat this as a comprehensive dictionary. Translation spells follow their printed rules, and no emotion makes you lose a language you know.

A few Simlish words are charming. Translate the actual plan for your party. They also need to know which door explodes.

Six places to build a longer story

Glimmerbrook: the door that keeps opening

A woodland town makes a good bridge between ordinary life and the Realm of Magic. Use a mentor, an overworked shopkeeper, and a neighbor who remembers when the portal was quiet. A local problem might begin with missing deliveries and grow into a dispute about who is responsible for keeping magical travel safe.

Useful locations: a repair counter crowded with broken wands, a streamside path, and a classroom with one locked cabinet. A difficult choice: close a dangerous route and strand a traveler, or keep it open long enough to attempt a rescue.

Forgotten Hollow: privacy is a local custom

Give the district a mixture of long-term residents and newcomers. The tension need not be “everyone is secretly a monster.” It can be about food supply, inheritance, trust, and what a small community owes somebody who wants to begin again. A Vampire Sim may know the etiquette while still lacking any supernatural authority over the town.

Useful locations: a night market, an immaculate public garden, and an archive that opens after sunset. A difficult choice: expose a useful person’s deception or protect their privacy while finding another way to stop the harm.

Sulani: the water connects everyone

Build the adventure around a community’s relationship with the sea rather than using the islands as an empty holiday backdrop. Fishing, conservation, travel, and family obligations can bring people into the same scene. A Mermaid’s underwater access helps them gather information, but a lasting solution usually needs cooperation above the surface too.

Useful locations: a communal meal, a damaged landing, and a reef affected by an unfamiliar substance. A difficult choice: protect a vital local livelihood while confronting the person whose business is damaging it.

Moonwood Mill: belonging is complicated

Make the competing groups understandable. One pack values established responsibilities; another believes those customs have left people out. A shared emergency can force them to work together. Werewolf characters can have distinctive customs and physical habits without compulsory violence, and non-werewolf neighbors deserve motives of their own.

Useful locations: a converted mill, a meeting place in the woods, and a workshop whose owner repairs everyone’s mistakes. A difficult choice: obey a tradition that keeps the peace or change it because it is failing somebody vulnerable.

StrangerVille: evidence before certainty

The plant mystery works when each clue changes the party’s understanding. Begin with behavior that is odd but not immediately hostile, then supply concrete signs of a shared cause. Give the laboratory staff conflicting obligations rather than identical villain speeches. Someone may have concealed evidence because they feared panic, not because they wanted the town harmed.

Useful locations: a small clinic, a sealed sample room, and a greenhouse with improvised containment. A difficult choice: release an incomplete warning now or spend precious time obtaining proof.

Sixam: visitors in the wrong catalogue

Let unfamiliar procedures create comedy without making every Alien foolish. A research station might have excellent instruments and terrible assumptions about the party’s social structure. A translation dispute, an incomplete map, or a quarantined sample can give each character a useful role. The strongest encounter may be persuading a conscientious scientist that their classification is wrong.

Useful locations: a transit platform, a carefully organized specimen archive, and an observation room facing an unfamiliar sky. A difficult choice: share information that helps an earnest researcher but could be used irresponsibly by their institution.

These expanded locations and conflicts are adventure material invented for this adaptation, not claims about every household or event in The Sims 4.

Bring a piece of home to Faerûn

Choose something small that survived the journey: a photograph, a key that opens nothing here, a packet of seeds, or a recipe written by somebody else. Introduce it during a quiet scene before making it the center of a quest. When it later matters, the party will remember why.

Likewise, let Faerûn change your Sim. They may learn to enjoy a festival, trust a local craftsperson, or discover that a room becomes home because people return to it. Returning to the Neighborhood can remain a goal without making the entire fantasy world a waiting room.

09

For the Dungeon Master

Keep the stakes. Keep the joke.

Fair rulings, ready-to-run scenes, and a three-session mini-adventure.

Player agency is always on

Free will is not a limited-use trait. A Sim chooses their actions, whether to socialize, and whom to trust. An aspiration, need, mood, or full moon never forces them to attack an ally, flirt, disclose a secret, or sabotage the party.

The jokes should create scenes everyone enjoys. Use awkward furniture, absurd paperwork, unreliable appliances, and misplaced confidence. Let players choose how personal comedy gets.

Death uses the actual death rules

At 0 Hit Points, use the campaign’s normal death saves, stabilization, healing, and instant-death rules. A Sim gets no free final Charisma check, automatic comeback, or postmortem action. Embarrassment, anger, laughter, and birthdays cannot kill a character through this handbook.

Grim can appear as a story character after a death. He has no invented Challenge Rating here. Bargaining may start a quest; it cannot bypass a resurrection spell’s cost or eligible targets.

Adapting Sims hazards
SceneAdjudicationKeep the joke
Kitchen fireUse a telegraphed fire hazard with ordinary damage and a clear way to escape or extinguish it.The Sim points at the stove. Their player may still take useful actions.
Broken pool ladderUse swimming, climbing, and suffocation rules. The pool edge is still a possible exit.The missing ladder is inconvenient, not a prohibition on climbing.
Faulty applianceExplain exposed wires, let it be disconnected, and use an appropriate trap if mishandled.The warranty expired during the portal incident.
Murphy bedTreat a visibly defective bed as a minor mechanical trap. Declare its trigger, detection DC, save, damage, and reset before use.The warning label is more expensive than the bed.
Spore exposureUse an encounter’s explicit effect and repeat saves. Provide clues, cures, and routes around the danger.An unnerving smile can be descriptive; permanent domination is not the default.
Rocket accidentSet stakes before the roll; use level-appropriate hazards and vehicle rules.A launch failure can explain planar travel without retroactively inflicting 10d6 damage.
What changed from the original handbook
  • Removed stacked species, aspiration, age, career, and mood ability increases.
  • Replaced unlimited emotional bonuses, automatic lie detection, and forced behaviors with normal checks and roleplay.
  • Made all eight occult ancestries mutually exclusive replacement packages. Spellcaster follows normal class progression.
  • Removed parallel rank resources, undefined “Ghost Points,” free spell upgrades, and opaque DC scaling.
  • Restored normal language magic, equipment training, healing, Concentration, and death rules.
  • Removed instant emotional deaths, rapid mandatory aging, infinite repair, free resurrection, and runaway gardening income.
  • Corrected the Forbidden Fruit and Ambrosia lore, and moved monster-grade abilities into DM material.

Balance still needs play at your table. After a few sessions, review how often a trait changes an outcome, whether occult choices dominate ordinary Sims, and whether any optional tracking slows the session.

Adjudicate ideas without rewarding vague declarations

Ask a player what they want to accomplish and how they attempt it. Choose the relevant rule or check only after those details are clear. A Sim who says “I improve the object” has not specified a result; a Sim who says “I brace the hinge so the door stays open during evacuation” has given you something concrete to resolve.

Use a check when success is uncertain and the outcome matters. If the right tool and enough safe time make a routine task straightforward, let it succeed. If a failed attempt would simply lead to the same roll again with no change, either resolve the task or introduce an actual cost or consequence before rolling. Skill Grind then has a clear role: it changes the outcome of one real attempt, not a process of rolling until the story gives up.

Three ready-to-run scene frames

Social / exploration · any level

The inspection is in twenty minutes

Situation. An inspector is arriving at the party’s rented house. A missing ledger, a loose banister, and an Angry Gnome all suggest the building is less ready than the landlord claims. The landlord can explain the stakes: a temporary closure would displace several tenants.

What the party can learn. The ledger is behind the boiler, the banister needs ordinary repair, and the gnome is agitated because somebody moved its pot. Those basic facts should be discoverable through sensible investigation. Checks determine speed, finesse, or whether a temporary fix is convincing; they do not gate the entire situation.

Choices. Repair honestly, admit the remaining problem and seek time, or conceal it and risk the relationship. The inspector is firm but reasonable. The gnome can be repositioned peacefully; if attacked, use its stat block. End with a clear consequence and a new household contact, not a compulsory fight over a municipal form.

Garden hazard · starting configuration for four level 3–4 characters

The cake beyond the fence

Situation. A missing delivery cart is beside one Cowplant. Its owner wants the goods recovered and the creature contained, not necessarily killed. Show the rooted stem, damaged fence, and a warning sign before anyone enters its reach.

Terrain. A clear path around the outside allows ranged attacks and observation. A low fence supplies a visible boundary rather than an invisible barrier. The cart is within the Cowplant’s reach, so recovering it quickly may require coordination.

Run it. Use the bestiary’s separate Bite and Swallow actions. Apply the lure’s limited movement and immunity after the save exactly as written. Allies have an opportunity to respond before a grappled creature is swallowed. State escape options clearly. The plant’s immobility makes preparation powerful; do not secretly add movement because the party found a safe angle.

Outcomes. Retrieving the cart, repairing the enclosure, or defeating the plant can each satisfy the immediate goal. Its owner may become a useful supplier. Treat the suggested level range as a starting point; examine the actual party, terrain, and current resources before running it.

Investigation / containment · tune the creature count to the party

The greenhouse that smiles back

Situation. Workers have begun leaving the greenhouse in unusually similar moods. Two visible Spore Nodes guard a leaking sample container; a separate worker outside can explain the first signs of trouble. The party needs to close the container and reach a safe exit.

Clues. Wilted labels, masks hung by the door, and a damaged ventilation handle reveal the problem without requiring one perfect roll. A successful relevant check can identify a safer approach or speed the repair. The nodes’ spores use their printed short-duration Poison effect, never permanent control of a player character.

Choices. Use the accessible outside controls, enter with a coordinated plan, destroy the nodes from range, or evacuate and obtain help. A hostile situation can become Initiative when timing matters. Resolve a practical sealing action as an appropriate task with declared stakes, not as an arbitrary immunity to plant magic.

Afterward. A supplier’s mark connects the sample to a larger shipment. The party now has an adventure lead and someone grateful enough to look after the garden while they follow it.

A three-session mini-adventure: The Missing Exit

A portal component has been installed in an ordinary neighborhood greenhouse. It is also the component the Sim needs to investigate the accident that brought them here. The landlord thought it was an energy-saving device. The installer was sincere, underqualified, and has left town.

  1. Session one: establish the household. Run the inspection scene and introduce a tenant, a supplier, and a helpful local craftsperson. The ledger or another plainly available clue identifies the greenhouse installation. Let the party decide whether to pursue it for safety, money, friendship, or a way home.
  2. Session two: trace the shipment. Follow records, interview the installer’s colleague, and recover the delivery cart from the Cowplant garden. Different approaches reveal the same essential lead: the component is amplifying an imported plant’s response to nearby magic. Additional success can identify the correct shutdown sequence or secure help.
  3. Session three: shut down safely. Use the greenhouse containment scene. The final choice is whether to remove the component immediately, risking damage to a promising route home, or stabilize the site long enough to gather better readings. Make the risks visible and let multiple plans work. The party’s research, relationships, and preparations determine what resources they bring.

Keep the absent installer available for a later conversation rather than automatically revealing a mastermind. A small mistake with a large consequence can support apology, repair, and future trust. Reward the adventure through the campaign’s ordinary advancement and treasure, plus a concrete change to the household.

Review balance using events, not impressions

After several sessions, note which traits changed a result, how often rests happened, whether an option repeatedly solved problems without a meaningful decision, and whether a player felt left out. Compare similar situations before changing a feature. A Mermaid dominating a single underwater scene is different from an ancestry dominating every combat.

Make one adjustment at a time, explain it before the next session, and let the affected player rebuild if the change alters their character concept. Do not correct an unexpectedly effective plan by adding a surprise permanent weakness. A playable handbook is a shared agreement, including when it needs revision.

10

Do not feed the furniture

Some neighbors bite.

Stat blocks, readable threats, and encounters with more than one solution.

These homebrew NPCs use their own stat blocks, not player species features. Challenge Ratings are provisional estimates. Terrain, party size, and prepared tactics matter, especially for immobile plants. Never add these traits to an occult character.

CowplantLarge Plant, UnalignedCR 3
AC 13HP 68 (8d10 + 24)Speed 0 ft.CR 3 (700 XP; PB +2)

Traits

Rooted. The Cowplant cannot move and cannot be moved against its will while rooted in soil.

Cake Lure. As a Bonus Action, if it has no creature swallowed, the Cowplant displays its cake. One creature it can see within 20 feet that can see the cake makes a DC 12 Wisdom save. On a failure, the target must use up to 10 feet of its movement toward the Cowplant on its next turn, avoiding obvious hazards; this effect then ends. A creature immune to Charmed automatically succeeds. After this save, the target is immune to this Cowplant’s lure for 24 hours.

Actions

Bite. Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage. A Medium or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 14). The Cowplant can grapple only one creature at a time.

Swallow. The Cowplant swallows one Medium or smaller creature Grappled by it. The grapple ends. The target is Blinded and Restrained, has Total Cover against effects outside the Cowplant, and takes 7 (2d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the Cowplant’s turns. It can hold one creature. A swallowed creature can use an action to make a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check, escaping into an unoccupied space within 5 feet on success. If the Cowplant takes 15 or more damage in a single turn from a creature inside it, it regurgitates that creature into such a space. Death releases its victim.

Running it. Bite and Swallow are separate actions, so the party has a turn to help. The lure does not force a creature to eat the cake. A rooted enemy rewards range and scouting; use it as a garden hazard, not a surprise execution.

Constructed Nature. The Servo does not require air, food, drink, or sleep. These are NPC traits and do not transfer to a Servo player character.

Actions

Running it. A durable guard with a telegraphed electrical discharge. No unlimited self-repair and no automatic water shutdown. These CRs are estimates for testing, not guarantees about difficulty.

The Mother Plant: build the encounter before the boss

For an immediately runnable version, reskin the Shambling Mound from the campaign’s monster rules as a mobile offshoot of the Mother. Use that stat block in full, without adding spore auras, Legendary Actions, charm, or extra resistances. Explain its Lightning interaction before combat through clues in the lab.

The immense, rooted Mother can remain the source of the outbreak and an adventure objective. Destroying containment relays, delivering a researched antidote, or evacuating the town can resolve the story. A custom legendary boss needs its own encounter design and playtest; this handbook does not assign a misleading CR to permanent mind control.

Voidcritters are companions, not free summons

Use a normal pet’s stat block for a mundane companion, or a permitted familiar stat block with Find Familiar. A card collection never grants extra creatures, actions, or combat powers.

Give the creatures a job in the scene

The Cowplant is strongest as a visible hazard with something valuable nearby. The Angry Gnome is a nuisance, a clue, or a small opponent who makes a mundane task stranger. The Spore Node is containment pressure. The Rogue Servo is a guard whose programming or owner might be part of the mystery. Naming that job helps you choose terrain and goals without adding unlisted powers.

Run the bestiary as encounters, not surprises
CreatureShow before the dangerTactics and counterplayAn outcome besides killing it
CowplantA rooted stalk, a convincing cake lure, and signs that something struggled nearby.It uses reach and the lure, then Bite and Swallow on separate actions. Distance, coordinated escape, and the enclosure matter.Recover the goods, repair containment, or arrange a qualified keeper.
Angry GnomeTiny footprints, moved ornaments, and a suspiciously deliberate hat.Keep its one attack and limited rattle small in scale. Its unobserved relocation is not a combat teleport.Put the disturbed object back, negotiate through its keeper, or leave it safely contained.
Spore NodeA visible growth, warning labels, and an understandable connection to the sample.Use the short-range puff and its recharge. Range and Fire vulnerability create obvious counters.Seal the sample, close the route, or bring a specialist after evacuation.
Rogue ServoRepeated patrol instructions, electrical warning lights, and a maintenance label.It follows its printed attacks and pulse. It cannot self-repair indefinitely or shut down automatically in a puddle.Fulfill a valid access procedure, identify its operator, or persuade somebody to revoke its order.

Construct an encounter around decisions

Choose the objective, the visible threat, the space, and an exit before placing opponents. Then compare the creatures to the campaign’s encounter guidance and the party’s actual level and resources. A fixed Challenge Rating cannot account for every interaction: an immobile creature across an open field is not the same problem as one in a narrow cellar.

For the Mother Plant, start with the existing offshoot reskin and the investigation that leads to it. If you later design a legendary boss, develop its damage, durability, control, and action economy together. Short repeatable saves, clear counterplay, and multiple meaningful objectives make a better finale than a hidden permanent-domination threshold.

11

At the table

Life, briefly under control.

Check in, make a note, and get back to the adventure.

A small, manual session aid. Nothing here changes your rules or advances with real time. Your choices are stored in this browser when storage is available; keep your main character sheet for combat numbers.

Live mode

Your Sim

Feeling Fine

Track innate spell uses on your character sheet if you chose an occult package.

Ready for this session

Long Rest resets Energy and the Skill Grind checkbox here. It does not automatically supply food, water, comfort, or the rest benefits on your main sheet.

Before you roll

  • Does a real rule grant this ability?
  • Is its action, target, range, and resource available?
  • Does it require Concentration or a component?
  • Is the mood just flavor? Usually, yes.

Then roll the normal dice. The plumbob believes in you.

Keep the session record short enough to use

At the end of play, record one discovery, one promise, one unresolved problem, and the next practical step. These are more helpful than a transcript. Keep combat resources on the actual character sheet, where you can distinguish class uses, innate free castings, item charges, and rest recovery.

A good note might read: “The greenhouse component matches Mira’s portal records. We promised Mara to recover the cart. The Cowplant fence is broken. Next: ask the keeper for the key and examine the warning signs before approaching.” That gives everyone a clear way back into the next session.

Reading & credits

The fine print, in human.

This is an unofficial fan adaptation. Sim-specific player options, items, NPCs, and adventure hooks here are homebrew, not canonical D&D mechanics or literal simulations of every Sims system. The Neighborhood-to-Faerûn connection is invented for this handbook.

  • SRD 5.2.1: the rules foundation; complete PDF for spells, items, monsters, and core rules.
  • Character origins and rules glossary: official reference for creation and rules terms.
  • EA gardening guide: Forbidden Fruit, PlantSims, and the temporary five-day transformation in The Sims 4.
  • EA death and revival guide: Ambrosia’s angelfish, Death Flower, and Potion of Youth ingredients. The item here is a separate D&D adaptation.

Class and build references

The twelve class guides summarize the 2024 rules in SRD 5.2.1, with links to each class’s full rules. Career paths, tactics, household scenes, and adventure material are original guidance for this adaptation. Starting builds use the SRD backgrounds, Origin feats, equipment options, and 27-point ability buy. Spell and feature text in the reference governs every detail.
